title: Structural induction on Boolean circuits
statement: Let $P$ be a property of Boolean circuits on $n$ variables. Suppose that $P$ holds for every literal circuit, and that whenever $P$ holds for every circuit in a list $cs$ of children, it also holds for the gate circuit $\mathrm{node}(isAnd, cs)$ formed from $cs$ (an AND gate when $isAnd = \mathrm{true}$, an OR gate when $isAnd = \mathrm{false}$). Then $P$ holds for every Boolean circuit on $n$ variables.
hypotheses_covered: base case: property holds for every literal circuit
step case: for every gate, if the property holds for all children in the list then it holds for the gate node
replaced:
An induction principle for \texttt{Circuit} stating that to prove a predicate
$\mathrm{motive}$ holds for every circuit it suffices to prove it for every literal and,
in the node case, to prove $\mathrm{motive}(\texttt{node}\,isAnd\,cs)$ assuming
$\mathrm{motive}\,c$ for every child $c \in cs$. This works around the lack of native
support for nested inductives.
